chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Maymun the goldsmith, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I undertake work in which there is goldsmithing and engraving, so I stipulate with the engraver on a condition. When the accounting comes between me and him, I make him reduce from the stipulated amount.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is that with his agreement?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.أُشَارِطُ: I stipulate / I make a contract

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sub-contract part of a trade job and deduct the cost from the original contract price?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of *al-musawamah* (contracting for work) and subsequent sub-contracting, provided the deduction from the original price is agreed upon by the subcontractor with a willing mind (*bi-tayyib nafs*). It highlights the flexibility in commercial partnerships within Shia jurisprudence, allowing for profit-sharing or cost-deduction models as long as there is no ambiguity (*gharar*) or coercion. The Imam’s simple affirmation underscores the general permissibility of such arrangements unless specific prohibitive conditions are met.
